open_points.subject: A11/A18 post-send persistence failure handling
open_points.text: A11 rule 1: "then one store call writes the outcome..."; A18 rule 3: "A call that fails changes nothing."
open_points.question: If the HTTP attempt has already been sent (or answered) but the outcome store call fails, what must the kernel do to preserve run/effect truth: stop the process, return refusal, or continue with an implicit recovery path?
options: Stop the kernel immediately so restart recovery turns the in-flight attempt into unknown
Return an internal refusal but keep process alive, leaving in-flight for startup recovery
Retry the same store call in-place until it succeeds
open_points.default_guess: Stop the kernel immediately and rely on startup recovery of in-flight attempts.

open_points.subject: A09 path placeholder parsing
open_points.text: A09 rule 2: "every `{name}` in the path takes the input port of that name"
open_points.question: What is the exact placeholder grammar and validation (unmatched braces, empty name, repeated placeholders, escaping literal braces)?
options: Define a strict placeholder grammar and refuse malformed paths at proposal time
Treat `{...}` by a simple substring scan and leave edge cases to runtime refusal
open_points.default_guess: Use a strict grammar and refuse malformed placeholder syntax during binding proposal.

open_points.subject: A07 execution-class computation for records with no data
open_points.text: A07 rule 5: "The class of an execution is the highest class among the values and files its NodeExecution or TrialExecution names as inputs, and for an operation also among its outputs"
open_points.question: What class is assigned when an execution record names no inputs and no outputs (for example `skipped_by_guard` / `upstream_failed` records without payload)?
options: Treat it as undefined and skip class-based redaction logic for such records

open_points.subject: A05 cycle-check scope
open_points.text: A05 phase 7: "cycles: the graph of nodes and edges is acyclic"
open_points.question: Does cycle detection include synthetic flow endpoints (empty-node flow input/output endpoints) or only real flow nodes?
options: Run cycle detection only on node-to-node dependency graph
Include flow input/output endpoints as vertices in the cycle graph
open_points.default_guess: Check cycles only among real flow nodes.
